course_description:
This course teaches students to critically pair creative content and information with digital media. It also introduces students to both analyse and create transmedia narratives, drawing on a variety of different genres and media platforms. In producing their own transmedia stories, students will hone a set of media production skills, including audio-visual digital media as well as verbal presentation skills.

As the media landscape evolves, the ability to craft stories across formats is essential for contemporary communicators. Through lectures, workshops, and industry examples, students examine how different media shape communication and narrative meaning. Working in creative teams, they develop an original transmedia storyworld using industry-standard tools, producing a media portfolio that showcases their ability to communicate ideas clearly and creatively across multiple platforms. The skills developed in this course are transferable to a wide range of professional contexts where compelling storytelling is essential.

ACTIVITIES ASSOCIATED WITH THIS COURSE
1 LECTURES:
We have face to face lectures starting in Week 1. The lectures will also be available as video recordings on Blackboard, after their scheduled time. Please try to attend lectures in person. This is another opportunity to engage with other students and ask questions to the lecturer.
You are expected to attend or watch the lectures BEFORE your assigned tutorial.
2 TUTORIALS:
Tutorials are where you discuss ideas with your colleagues and tutors and get feedback on your work. Please ensure that you successfully sign up for a tutorial (T Group) in Allocate by the first week of class and show up to that same tutorial and that tutorial only throughout the semester. Tutorials commence in Week 2. If you show up to a tutorial you are not enrolled in, you will be asked to leave.
The tutorials are organised around smaller cohorts (20-25 students) and will involve more hands-on group exercises and learning that incorporates ongoing tutor feedback. If you do not attend any tutorials by Tutorial 4, you will be in danger of failing the course entirely and may be advised to withdraw.
Each week you are asked to complete a module on Blackboard and come to the tutorial prepared. The modules introduce key concepts in transmedia theory and related ideas and how to work across multiple media formats. They also give you important case studies and examples that will help you generate ideas for your own work.
Missing tutorials:
When you skip class you miss time to work with your creative team, and important information and discussions designed to help you do well in the assessments.
3 PRODUCTION SKILLS WORKSHOPS:
The main technical software and media production skills are taught through workshops offered by an on-campus department called
Jactech
. These workshops are offered outside scheduled tutorials and lectures. This will be discussed in further detail at the first lecture.
course_aims: This course develops your capacity to work purposefully and critically across multiple media platforms, building the analytical and creative skills to select, adapt, and distribute content in ways that serve both the story and the audience. Working in creative teams, you will design and develop an original transmedia storyworld from concept to execution.

learning_outcomes.description: Demonstrate understanding of how creative content behaves in different media contexts and adapts to different understandings of user engagement.
Collaborate effectively in creative teams across the full semester, with documented individual contribution to group concept development.
Produce original media assets that showcase a transmedia storyworld, drawing on practices such as photography, graphic design, illustration, and audio-visual production.
Critically justify creative decisions, including reflection on authentic authorship, applying transmedia concepts and relevant theoretical ideas covered in the course.

assessment_details.title: Portfolio Consultations
assessment_details.due_date: Week 5 - Week 12 The due date for your AI Charter (A1 Part A) and Portfolio (A1 Part B) is BEFORE your tutorial when your consultation is due.
assessment_details.task_description: This assessment involves two consultations with your tutor, scheduled during tutorial time: Assessment 1 Part A = 15% Assessment 1 Part B = 20% These consultations are centred around the students’ media portfolio work. Students will explain and justify their creative and technical decisions, demonstrating critical analysis skills developed in the course, by using concepts and vocabulary pertinent to transmedia storytelling. Assessment 1 Part A (15%) Assessment 1 Part A has 2 components: AI Charter and Portfolio Consultation. AI CHARTER: As a team you will write an AI Charter and submit it individually to Turnitin. The AI Charter is a written team agreement that establishes how your group will and will not use artificial intelligence tools throughout this project. It should address: Authorship: Where does your creative contribution end and AI assistance begin? Use agreements: Which tools, if any, will you use, and for what specific tasks? What will you not use AI for? The charter will be revisited in Assessment 3, where you will reflect on how your actual AI use compared to your original commitments. PORTFOLIO CONSULTATION: As a team, you will describe what your transmedia project is. Individually, each team member will explain: What is your unique contribution to your team’s transmedia project What have you done so far, what are your plans for Assessment 2 submission and how you plan to explore your medium’s strengths. Marking split: Team components (AI charter + project concept question) are marked as a team (50%); individual responses receive individual marks (50%). Conditions: Portfolio consultations happen at students' tables: this is not a formal presentation. All materials (phones, notebooks) should be packed away before the consultation begins. Teams may use one slide on a laptop or one printed visual aid. If a laptop is used, the screen should be visible to all team members at all times. Visual aids are support tools only and are not assessed. No notes or machine translation tools may be used during the consultation. Assessment 1 Part B (20%) The second portfolio consultation is entirely individual and will happen on week 11 or 12. A schedule will be made available on Blackboard. During this consultation, you will explain how you are responding to the feedback you received on Assessment 2, and how that response is shaping your Assessment 3 submission. Conditions: BEFORE your consultation, you must submit at least one media asset to Blackboard that demonstrates how you are addressing your Assessment 2 feedback. You may refer to this submission during the consultation. If you have not submitted anything to Blackboard by the time your tutor calls you for your consultation, you will not be permitted to sit the consultation. No notes or machine translation tools may be used during the consultation. Full details and a comprehensive grading rubric are provided on Blackboard under "Assessments". assessment_details.title: Midsemester Project: Media Portfolio + Statement
assessment_details.task_description: You will work in a creative team (4 students) to create a transmedia storyworld that exists authentically across multiple platforms. Each team member is responsible for one platform/medium, ensuring that the story elements respond and capitalise on each medium’s unique features (medium specificity). Assessment components (submitted individually on Blackboard): Media portfolio (work-in-progress stage) Process Evidence Media Strategy Statement 1 Media Portfolio: Each person in the team must produce a media portfolio of creative and original work using the Adobe Suite flagship programs (Photoshop, Premiere Pro, Audition, Illustrator, InDesign). We want you to use these software because they are the industry standard. At this point, we are interested in work-in-progress stage of your media portfolio. The final version will be submitted in Assessment 3. You can use a variety of different formats, such as drawing and illustration, still photography, posters, audio-visual material, including video and podcast, social media account, game prototype, among others. We are open to your ideas! Examples of adequately substantial individual media portfolio submitted at the mid-semester stage will be discussed in tutorials and lectures. Original content only: No stock images or footage (except scoring/music). Only content produced during the period of this course (no old pictures/footage). 2 Process Evidence: You must provide clear evidence of your creative and technical process. This evidence should allow markers to verify that you have used the Adobe Creative suite and that you are using your own images . You process evidence document should demonstrate: How you created your media portfolio. How the Adobe Suite was used. Did you use AI or Machine Translation tools at any stage? If yes, specify which tools, how, and why, and what parts of the work are fully your own and what parts are AI generated. Was it helpful? How? Justify the use of these tools. Examples of evidence includes, but are not limited to: Screenshots of Adobe timelines/layers Drafts, early exports, failed tests Time lapse of your drawing / editing Original assets files Version history 3 Media Strategy Statement: You must submit a written statement (500 words) addressing the following questions: What is your team storyworld about? How is your media output contributing to your team's storyworld? How are you capitalising on medium specificity? How have the course’s ideas informed your work? Full details and a comprehensive grading rubric are provided on Blackboard under "Assessments". Read full task description Hide full task description

assessment_details.title: Final Project: Media Portfolio + Statement
assessment_details.task_description: The final project is your final media portfolio, ready for publication, that should incorporate feedback from previous assessments. Assessment 3 components (submitted individually on Blackboard): Media portfolio (Final version, ready to be published). Process Evidence Media Strategy Statement + AI Charter update Peer Assessment Statement 1 Media Portfolio: This is your final work, ready to released into the world. At this stage, the individual portfolio should demonstrate noticeable improvement from the Assessment 2, including new media developed since the midterm, pushing your storyworld concept further. You are expected to work with the Adobe Suite flagship programs (Photoshop, Premiere Pro, Audition, Illustrator, InDesign) in the production of your portfolio. Examples of adequately substantial individual final media portfolios will be discussed in tutorials and lectures. Original content only: No stock images or footage (except scoring/music). Only content produced during the period of this course (no old pictures/footage). 2 Process Evidence: You must provide clear evidence of your creative and technical process. This evidence should allow markers to verify that you have used the Adobe Creative suite and that you are using your own images . You process evidence document should demonstrate: How you created your media portfolio. How the Adobe Suite was used. Did you use AI or Machine Translation tools at any stage? If yes, specify which tools, how, and why, and what parts of the work are fully your own and what parts are AI generated. Was it helpful? How? Justify the use of these tools. Examples of evidence includes, but are not limited to: Screenshots of Adobe timelines/layers Drafts, early exports, failed tests Time lapse of your drawing / editing Original assets files Version history 3 Media Strategy Statement + AI Charter Update: Your media strategy statement (700 words) should explain: What did you make and how is this portfolio part of a transmedia project? How does your media output foster active participation? How did the AI Charter work for you and your team? Would you review/modify the charter? How? 4 Peer Assessment Statement: A statement (300 words) addressing the group dynamics: How did you work with your team to accomplish this task? And did this approach work well? Were there any issues with collaboration, and if so, how were they managed? What challenges did you face, and what might you do differently next time? learning_activities.topic: Week 1 Lecture: What is transmedia?
Week 1: No Tutorials Tutorials start in week 2.
Week 2 Lecture: Worldbuilding
Week 2 Tutorial: Forming transmedia teams Transmedia creative teams will be formed. You will begin creating your storyworld.
Week 3: NO LECTURE DUE TO PUBLIC HOLIDAY
Week 3: NO TUTORIALS DUE TO PUBLIC HOLIDAY You are encouraged to review the Blackboard content and seek inspiration for your transmedia storyworld and individual submission.
Week 4 Lecture: What makes a story?
Week 4 Tutorial: Creating your own story What transmedia story are you going to explore in this course? How? Crafting your AI charter. What is the role of AI in your creative process?
Week 5 Lecture: Transmedia and medium specificty
Week 5 Tutorial: Assessment 1 Part A - Portfolio consultations In-class group consultations with your tutor.
Week 6 Lecture: Transmedia principles: spreadability and distribution
Week 6 Tutorial: Practising transmedia principles How can you put transmedia principles into practice in your transmedia project?
Week 7 Lecture: Branding
Week 7 Tutorial: Auditing your storyworld Are you ready for Assessment 2? Does your team have a strong story concept? What elements of the course are you putting into practice?
Week 8 Lecture: Industry perspective (guest lecture) You will hear from an industry practitioner about the realities of professional media production across multiple platforms and formats.
Week 8 Tutorial: What can we learn from brands that do transmedia well? Which strategies can you apply to your transmedia project?
Week 9 Lecture: Subjectivity and bodies
Week 9 Tutorial: Thinking about your audience Who is your audience? Who is represented in your story? And how?
MIDSEMESTER BREAK
Week 10 Lecture: Participation and performance
Week 10 Tutorial: How can we make our audience feel part of our storyworld? Easter eggs, co-creation and more.
Week 11 Lecture: Transmedia in practice
Week 11 Tutorial: A1 Part B - Portfolio consultations In-class individual consultations with your tutor. You will be allocated to week 11 OR week 12.
Week 12 Lecture: Review / Answering your questions
Week 12 Tutorial: A1 Part B - Portfolio consultations In-class individual consultations with your tutor. You will be allocated to week 11 OR week 12.
Week 13: No classes

policies_and_procedures: University policies and procedures apply to all aspects of student life. As a UQ student, you must comply with University-wide and program-specific requirements, including the: Student Code of Conduct Policy Student Integrity and Misconduct Policy and Procedure Assessment Procedure Examinations Procedure Reasonable Adjustments for Students Policy and Procedure AI for Assessment Guide Recording of Teaching Policy and Procedure Learn more about UQ policies on my.UQ and the Policy and Procedure Library . Course guidelines Communication Expectations While you are a student at UQ, all communication must be conducted according to the UQ Student Code of Conduct . The UQ Library has a helpful Communicate and collaborate online module . Email is the primary way for you to send messages to, and receive information from, the School and our staff. You must use your UQ email address (not a private address) to communicate with staff. You should add a clear subject line, including course code, and a 2-3 word statement. You can send email at any time, however, please do not expect responses outside normal working hours (Monday to Friday from ~8am to ~5pm). Emails that constitute bullying, harassment or discrimination against staff contravene the Student Code of Conduct. Emails like this will be reported to the University, and the matter will be pursued as misconduct. Learning activities
